title: Perf benchmarking sync - 2026-05-19
content:
Attendees: Aisha, Ethan, Lina, Omar, Priya

Agenda:
- Quick recap of last week
- Recent regressions observed on prod-like perf runs
- Test-run artifacts and discrepancies between CI and canary
- Action items and roll-forward/backout thresholds

TL;DR:
- We observed a throughput drop (~20%) and increased p99 latency on a subset of quantized models after the fused-kernel changes merged in PR #4109. Impact is most visible on A100 nodes with CUDA 12.2 driver 535.54; older kernels (CUDA 11.x) do not show regression.
- Canary customers flagged elevated tail-latency for short prompts (<=128 tokens) when continuous batching is enabled.
- Repro steps and run artifacts are in the linked gs:// path. Next steps: quick rollback candidate, targeted microbench, driver validation, and additional telemetry on batching boundaries.

Notes / Discussion:
1) Repro summary:
   - Model: redwood-7b-q4_0 (quantized)
   - HW: A100-80GB (nvlink), driver: 535.54, CUDA 12.2
   - Config: seq_len=512, batch_sizes tested = [1,4,8], continuous_batching on, kv-cache enabled
   - Baseline (before PR 4109): throughput ~3200 tokens/sec, p50=18ms, p95=45ms, p99=78ms (batch=8, seq=512)
   - Current (after PR 4109 merge): throughput ~2500 tokens/sec, p50=25ms, p95=65ms, p99=120ms (same test)
   - Short prompt case (seq<=128, batch=8): p99 jumped from ~40ms -> ~95ms

2) Hypothesis and root-cause leads:
   - Fused-kernel codepath may be introducing additional kernel launch overhead for small sequences (observed more in short prompts).
   - CUDA driver 535.54 has different scheduling characteristics; similar regressions not seen on machines with CUDA 11.8 + driver 515.x.
   - Continuous batching interacts with new batching boundary logic in PR 4109; microbench indicates extra memcpy or synchronization at batch flush boundaries in certain codepaths.

3) Data artifacts and CI mismatch:
   - CI microbench uses a synthetic load that pads sequences to uniform length; our canary traffic has mixed lengths causing more boundary events. That explains why CI green but canary regressed.
   - Logged runs: gs://redwood-benchmarks/2026-05-19/run-57/ (full perf logs + flamegraphs). Summary JSON in linked_artifacts.

4) Immediate mitigation options (discussed):
   - Rollback PR 4109 on canary and observe impact (fast, but loses fused-kernel perf improvements on some workloads). Assigned: Ethan (rollback canary today)
   - Re-run microbench with driver 535.86 (newer driver candidate) across A100 fleet to see if drivers mitigate. Assigned: Lina (run-driver-matrix)
   - Add extra telemetry for batching boundary events and kernel durations (instrument continuous batching path). Assigned: Omar (telemetry spike)
   - Temporary config tweak: disable continuous batching for low-latency customers or set max-batch-wait to 5ms. Assigned: Priya (customer config PR)

5) Proposed test plan (short-term, 48-72h):
   - Day 0: Ethan rolls back PR 4109 on one canary cluster; run load tests mirrored from prod for 6 hours; capture p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and kernel timings.
   - Day 1: Lina runs driver matrix: 515.x, 525.x, 535.54, 535.86 on staging A100 nodes using same run harness (run-57).
   - Day 1-2: Omar pushes batching boundary telemetry to canary for 24h; correlate increased p99 with boundary events.
   - Day 2: If rollback restores baseline, we prepare a targeted revert PR and add additional unit/integration tests to cover small-seq fused-kernel path.

6) Results to capture in each run (minimum):
   - tokens/sec (avg), p50/p95/p99 latencies (ms), gpu_util (%), host_cpu_util (%), avg kernel launch time (us), memcpy times, number of batch flush events per second.
   - Save flamegraph and nvprof summary.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is the regressions limited to quantized models (q4_0) or also seen on q8_0 / fp16? Quick check: we saw smaller impact on fp16 (approx 5% drop), so quantized path seems hit harder.
- Are there any hardware-specific firmware differences between our A100 hosts? Need inventory check.
- Does the memory allocator change in PR 4109 interact with our custom pinned buffer pool?

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Ethan: rollback PR 4109 on canary + smoke test (due 2026-05-19 EOD) [blocker if fail to rollback cleanly]
- Lina: driver matrix runs + upload summaries to gs:// (due 2026-05-20)
- Omar: implement batching-boundary telemetry + short-term dashboard (due 2026-05-20)
- Priya: prepare customer config PR (disable continuous batching for low-latency tier) and coordinate with CS for affected customers (due 2026-05-21)
- Aisha: draft postmortem template and schedule deep-dive if rollback doesn't fully resolve (due 2026-05-21)

Meeting cadence / next sync:
- Hold follow-up sync Monday 2026-05-22 10:00 PT (30m) to review rollback results and driver matrix. If rollback fixes, plan for targeted revert + test coverage PR.

Notes to self / quick commands used for local repro:
- run harness: ./bench/run_perf.py --model redwood-7b-q4_0 --seq-len 512 --batch 8 --continuous-batching --warmup 200 --steps 1000 --out gs://redwood-benchmarks/2026-05-19/run-57
- nvprof collection: nvprof --profile-from-start off --log-file nvprof-run-57.txt ./bench/run_perf.py ...
- compare baseline: scripts/compare_runs.py gs://redwood-benchmarks/baseline-2026-04-15/summary.json gs://redwood-benchmarks/2026-05-19/run-57/summary.json

Appendix (raw numbers excerpt):
- baseline (batch=8, seq=512): tokens/sec=3200, p50=18, p95=45, p99=78
- current (batch=8, seq=512): tokens/sec=2500, p50=25, p95=65, p99=120
- short (batch=8, seq=64): tokens/sec=4100 -> 3600, p99 40 -> 95

If you have more data (fp16 runs, other drivers), paste into the run-57 folder or ping here.

-- Aisha
